This is awesome! As someone who plays Ingress (kinda bored with it, but it's still fun when traveling to a new place) and started playing Pokemon the day it was released in the US, I'm really excited about this. I really hope they build in the kind of experience curves that Ingress has; you actually have to spend weeks and months leveling up, not just a few hours. It would make it a lot more like a real-life experience; pokemon are hard to get, and take a long time to train, making each one valuable, even if it doesn't have perfect stats/movepool.

I hope they actually make you travel around to find different Pokemon. This could encourage people to become more active and get outside, even if it is just for a video game.

I also hope that this, like a lot of apps, limits the amount of activity you can do at a time without having to pay for more

Yes, the travel part is the most exciting feature, actually having to go look for Pokemon. That's the way ingress works; you have to travel to a specific location, and you can only gain experience from that place once before it 'overheats' and becomes unavailable to you for the next four hours. Ideally there would be different pokemon of different rarities in different locations, and you can only encounter them by walking around in that area. And once you've fought them, they wouldn't appear for a while, forcing you to travel to new places instead of just running in circles. Perhaps there's only one of each pokemon, and if they faint, they have to recover. If you catch them, then you can't catch anymore from that place and have to go somewhere else.

As far as price, I'm hoping it's a one-time app purchase deal, or you only have to pay for aesthetic upgrades, or maybe a low-cost monthly subscription. The great part about Ingress is that it's free, so the only advantage comes from experience and time invested in the game.
